    "rationale": "Iteration 0 raced 60 trials across oval, s-bend and slalom, with no finishes. Every run ended off track at progress 0.107 to 0.153, with one line-loss event each and max error 0.060 to 0.069 m. The off-track limit for this body is 0.06 m, so the robot loses the line and drifts out rather than stalling. Steering oscillation was highest on the slalom (0.153) and s-bend (0.143), and lowest on the oval (0.072).\n\nGeometry: I adopted the Builder's iteration 1 layout. Sensors sit at x = -0.02 to +0.02 in 10 mm steps, at y = 0.04, with 12 mm footprints. This narrows the row and moves it closer to the axle, which reduces sensing lag. With a 12 mm footprint on a 25 mm tape, a sensor at lateral position x sees the line while the robot's offset d satisfies |x - d| < about 0.0185. The outermost sensor therefore keeps the line until d is about 0.0385 m, before the 0.06 m off-track limit. The wide row of iteration 0 held the line only to about 0.058 m, so it gave almost no warning.\n\nController: the narrower row roughly doubles the steering gain per metre of offset if the weights stay at ±1. I halved the weights to (-0.5, -0.25, 0, 0.25, 0.5) so that the signal per metre of offset matches iteration 0 (kp = 2, weights ±1 over ±0.04 m). I kept kp at 2 and added a little damping (kd 0.3, from 0.2) to address the slalom oscillation. I reduced base_speed from 1.6 to 1.4 because the early drift happens at bends and speed feeds directly into centrifugal drift. ki stays at 0. line_loss stays at last_direction, since it has been the recovery behaviour in all runs so far.\n\nExpected result (not yet measured): fewer off-track endings and higher progress. Completion is still unlikely, because the robot must cover about 1.5 m/s on average, and the lower base_speed works against that. The race will show whether the line loss now comes from a bend or from start-up.",
